articles.title: Music Assistant stops favourites changing other household accounts
articles.dek: Favourite and library edits stay in the listener’s connected accounts; the app’s heart indicators remain shared.
body: Music Assistant stops one household member’s favourite and library changes from being copied into other people’s music-service accounts. A shared library item could carry links to several accounts, so starring a track or removing it from the library affected them all.

Contributor pcc0x limits those changes to the listener’s own sources and permitted whole-home sources, extending the account controls reported on September 13. In the reported family setup, one click marked a song as a favourite in three separate Navidrome accounts.

The correction protects the connected accounts. The heart shown inside Music Assistant remains shared between users; this does not introduce personal favourites within its own interface. Marcel van der Veldt reviewed the work.

pullRequests.title: Scope favorite and library writes to the sources the acting user may write to

articles.title: ESPHome keeps NFC readers working and reports failed tag writes
articles.dek: Tag handling fixes stop missed scans, repeated events and false success messages across three reader families.
body: ESPHome corrects failures that could stop PN7150 and PN7160 NFC readers detecting tags or make a tag left in place repeatedly appear to arrive and leave. PN532 readers also stop reporting failed tag writes as successful, and avoid restarting midway through formatting an NTAG215 tag.

Keith Burzinski also closes a memory-reading flaw in PN7150 and PN7160 card emulation, where the ESPHome device presents itself as a tag. A nearby reader could request data beyond the intended message; requests now stay within its bounds. Existing YAML settings stay the same.
Burzinski tested physical ESP32 setups with all three reader families, including tag reads and writes.

pullRequests.title: [pn71xx] Fix NCI transport and card emulation bugs; share code between PN7150 and PN7160
[pn532] Check InDataExchange status and fix tag handling

articles.title: Home Assistant gives AI assistants a choice before playing media
articles.dek: Separate search and playback tools replace a shortcut that always played the first match.
body: Home Assistant gives AI assistants a choice of media search results before starting playback. The previous combined tool automatically played the first match; separate tools let the assistant inspect the results and choose one that fits the request.

Paulus Schoutsen returns up to 20 playable matches with their titles and media types. The tools work with exposed players that support both searching and playback; the assistant is told to play a selected result on the player that supplied it.

pullRequests.title: Add dedicated media search and play LLM tools

articles.title: Music Assistant keeps search results handy while building playlists
articles.dek: Result menus and a remembered search keep tracks within reach while a playlist takes shape.
body: Music Assistant lets listeners add tracks to playlists directly from search results instead of repeatedly closing the search, adding an item and searching again. The result menu also offers playback, favourites and library actions, with a right-click on desktop or a press and hold on touchscreens.

The search remembers its query, selected tab, sources, results and scroll position when it closes or a result is opened. Marcel van der Veldt also gives desktop results more room and changes music searches to run with Enter or the Search button. OzGav supplies the item menus.

pullRequests.title: A bigger global search that remembers your last search
Add the item menu to search results
Hide play button on non-playable search results

articles.title: ESPHome reads Xiaomi S200 and S400 scales over Bluetooth
articles.dek: Weight readings come from both models, with heart rate and impedance readings from the S400.
body: ESPHome adds local readings from Xiaomi Smart Scale S200 and Body Composition Scale S400 devices. Both supply weight and the scale’s user-profile number; the S400 also supplies heart rate, two electrical-impedance readings and an indication that a measurement is complete.

The component listens to the scale’s encrypted Bluetooth broadcasts and needs its encryption key to read them. Dckiller supplies the component and companion guide. The readings do not include calculated body-composition estimates.

pullRequests.title: [xiaomi_body_scale] Add Xiaomi body scale S200 and S400
[xiaomi_body_scale] Add Xiaomi body scale S200 and S400 documentation

articles.title: Home Assistant opens Shelly radiator valves to other Shelly gateways
articles.dek: Compatible Gen2 and newer Shelly devices can act as gateways with firmware 2.1.
body: Home Assistant broadens its support for Shelly BLU TRV radiator valves connected through compatible Shelly Gen2 and newer devices, instead of requiring the dedicated BLU Gateway. Those alternative gateways need Shelly firmware 2.1.
Maciej Bieniek extends Home Assistant’s calibration control and handling of removed valves to those alternative gateways, building on the supporting aioshelly library change.

pullRequests.title: Allow integration of the Shelly BLU TRV via a device other than the BLU Gateway
Free Blu TRV from Blu Gateway

articles.title: Home Assistant removes phone connection credentials from a debug message
articles.dek: A sensitive webhook identifier is replaced with the ordinary entity name when pending sensor updates are logged.
body: Home Assistant stops including a phone’s sensitive webhook identifier in a debug message about pending sensor updates. People sharing those logs for troubleshooting no longer expose that identifier through this message.

Franck Nijhof keeps the sensor’s ordinary entity identifier and update data in the log. Current companion apps also require encrypted updates, so the webhook identifier alone is not enough to inject readings into those registrations. Registrations without encryption lack that additional protection.

pullRequests.title: Stop logging the webhook ID in mobile_app pending updates

articles.title: Home Assistant can share new AI tools with external assistants
articles.dek: New server setups automatically include later toolsets, while existing setups retain their chosen selection.
body: Home Assistant’s Model Context Protocol server gains an option to include every registered set of AI tools, including ones added later. External AI assistants can discover those toolsets without someone returning to select each new one.

New server setups use this option by default and continue to require an administrator account. Existing setups retain their selected interfaces. Turning off “Expose all LLM APIs” in the integration’s configuration restores an explicit selection.

pullRequests.title: Add option to expose all LLM APIs in the MCP server

articles.title: Music Assistant resumes at the right point after announcements
articles.dek: Players without native announcement support stop skipping ahead when the message ends.
body: Music Assistant keeps a track’s place while an announcement interrupts playback. On Squeezelite and other players using its fallback announcement path, the playback clock could keep advancing during the message, making the track jump ahead or effectively restart when music resumed.
Michael Shaffer stops the active queue before the announcement and resumes from the saved position. This is his first contribution to the Music Assistant server, reviewed by Fabian Munkes.

pullRequests.title: Fix resume position after fallback announcements

articles.title: Home Assistant controls one-touch locking on compatible Matter locks
articles.dek: A configuration switch chooses whether a keypad touch can lock the door without a PIN.
body: Home Assistant adds a setting for one-touch locking on Matter locks that expose the option. It controls whether someone can lock the door with a single keypad touch without entering a PIN; it does not enable PIN-free unlocking.
Mark Spatz tested the switch on a Yale Matter lock, where disabling it stopped a touch on the logo from locking the door. This is his first contribution to Home Assistant Core.

pullRequests.title: Add Matter door lock one-touch locking switch

articles.title: Home Assistant identifies Brother paper jams and empty supplies
articles.dek: Dedicated problem readings distinguish paper, door and ink or toner faults on supported printers.
body: Brother printers gain dedicated Home Assistant readings for a paper jam, an open door, missing paper and low or empty ink or toner. These on-or-off problem indicators give dashboards and automations separate conditions to watch.
Maciej Bieniek adds further tray and maintenance warnings that start disabled. The readings appear only on printers that supply the required error information.

pullRequests.title: Add a binary sensor platform to the Brother integration

articles.title: Assist adds Greek fan-mode commands and clearer room cleaning
articles.dek: Climate controls work by name, room or floor, while a cleaning request targets the requested area.
body: Greek speakers gain Assist commands for setting a climate device’s fan mode, including requests directed at a named device, room or floor. The language rules also distinguish asking a robot vacuum to clean a room from starting a vacuum that is located there.

Contributor apo-mak expands timer extensions that combine hours, minutes and seconds, position commands that specify a room or floor, and temperature questions for a floor. These additions extend existing Greek voice control.
